patient_information: A 22-year-old woman from Ashulia near Dhaka, Bangladesh.
chief_complaint: A history of passing 12 to 15 large-volume stools resembling diluted milk or rice water with white flakes in the past day, leading to unresponsiveness.
history_of_present_illness: A 22-year-old woman presented with 12 to 15 large-volume stools in the past day, which resembled diluted milk or rice water with white flakes. She became unresponsive about an hour prior to hospital admission. She had not complained of pain and did not have fever.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient recently attended a religious festival where water was supplied in large metal containers. Her husband reported that five or six other attendees were also ill with diarrhoea. The infection was most likely acquired from contaminated water consumed from these containers during the festival, indicating a typical cholera outbreak with potential for further spread if control measures are not rapidly instituted.
vitals: Her pulse rate is 110 bpm, low volume, and her blood pressure is 90/50 mmHg.
physical_exam: A thin young woman, stuporous and responding minimally to a painful stimulus (GCS 9/15). She was afebrile, with sunken eyes, dry mouth, and a scaphoid abdomen. A skin pinch returned very slowly. The remainder of her systemic examination was normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results on admission showed Sodium 143.8 mmol/L (Reference 135-145 mmol/L), Potassium 3.0 mmol/L (Reference 3.5-5.0 mmol/L), Chloride 103.8 mmol/L (Reference 98-108 mmol/L), Bicarbonate 11.4 mmol/L (Reference 23-28 mmol/L), Lactic acid (venous) 4.1 mmol/L (Reference 0.67-1.8 mmol/L), Creatine 203 µmol/L (Reference 62-115 µmol/L), and Blood Urea Nitrogen 8.6 mmol/L (Reference 2.9-7.1 mmol/L). Macroscopic stool examination revealed liquid, rice-water appearance with no faecal matter. Hanging drop preparation showed small slender curved bacilli with darting motility, which was completely inhibited by Vibrio cholerae antiserum O1. Stool culture grew V. cholerae (Fig. 14.1), and the organism was typed as V. cholerae O1, Serotype Ogawa, biotype El Tor.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient was admitted and immediately started on intravenous rehydration with Ringer's lactate solution. After 3 L in the first hour, her pulse rate improved to 84 bpm and blood pressure to 100/70 mmHg. Over the next 3 hours, an additional 2L was administered, and she became alert and responsive. She was then started on oral rehydration and given a single dose of 300 mg doxycycline. She was discharged on the third day once stool consistency had returned to normal. Local health authorities identified an additional 44 cases of cholera, all of whom were treated, received health education, and had overhead tanks chlorinated.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis is cholera, caused by Vibrio cholerae O1, Serotype Ogawa, biotype El Tor. This was supported by clinical presentation of profuse watery diarrhea with severe dehydration, laboratory findings of electrolyte derangements, and confirmed by stool examination showing darting motile bacilli inhibited by V. cholerae antiserum O1, and subsequent culture growing V. cholerae.
